newsitem.title: GERMANY: German oilseeds lobby rejects EU aid cut plan.
newsitem.headline: German oilseeds lobby rejects EU aid cut plan.

text.p: Germany's Union for the Promotion of Oil and Protein Crops (Ufop) on Friday rejected plans by the European Commission to cut aid for land set-aside by 27 percent in 1997/98 (July/June).
A statement from the producer funded lobby said it was "vehemently" opposed to the Commission's plans, which were tabled on March 5 within a package of arable area cuts.
Ufop chairman Klaus Kliem said, "The proposed cut threatens the future of industrial crops on set-aside land."
Kliem also rejected the planned cuts of 7.3 and 4.2 percent respectively in cereals and oilseed base area aid.
He urged the farm ministers council meeting, scheduled for March 17-18, to throw out the proposals.
He called on ministers to protect initiatives to boost the production and marketing of industrial raw materials made from renewable resources, which farmers may grow on set-aside land.
Farmers needed to plan their sowings well in advance and withdrawing support for this newly-developed sector would be a breach of trust, Kliem said.

If 300,000 hectares of rapeseed cultivation for alternative biodiesel were withdrawn, this would negatively affect some 5,000 jobs, taxes and social security contributions derived from jobs in processing and distribution of such fuels.
